issue_context.title: Child Scene nodes disappearing from loaded/instantiated PackedScenes
issue_context.body: ### Tested versions - not reproducible 4.3 stable - reproducible 4.4 beta 1 ### System information MacOS 15.2 Godot4.4 Beta 1 ### Issue description Child scene nodes disappearing after loading of a packed scene. [Example Repo](https://github.com/mrmikemon/scenetest4_4beta1.git) ### Steps to reproduce [Example Repo](https://github.com/mrmikemon/scenetest4_4beta1.git) Test code 1. Finds a place holder node in main scene 2. Removes the placehodler node 'LoadedLevel' 3. Loads a packed scene from resoure and instanciate 4. Rename the scene as 'LoadedLevel' Snapshot of tree just after load Snapshot once main scene displayed Test result Level loads correctly All child node instanciate All child scenes 'BaseStation' child scenes are removed from scene only leaving simple nodes Verified using RemoteDebug view of node treee. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [Example Repo](https://github.com/mrmikemon/scenetest4_4beta1.git)
comments:
Your BaseStations are getting freed because `explosion`'s `GpuParticles3D.finished` signal is being incorrectly emitted (that's a bug), and this method is connected to it:
```gdscript
#res://basestation/basestation.gd
func _on_explosion_finished() -> void:
	queue_free()
```

This should already be fixed by #101596.

This bugged `GpuParticles3D.finished` emission should happen only in 4.4.beta1, should not happen in 4.4.dev7, should not happen in not yet released 4.4.beta2.

I just realized, we may not want to use `set_seed` here as it will change the value that gets saved if `seed` is serialized. 

We probably just want to call the renderingserver function directly
Hey @clayjohn i see you approved and left a review. Maybe it's just a bug on my end but it says you still approve. Do you want me to make these changes you suggested?
Got back to my PC this morning.  I'll go update this as well :)

Examining the code, I'm actually not sure about this change.  I see there is a public ``get_seed`` function.  So if I were to call ``RS::get_singleton()->particles_set_seed`` without also calling ``seed = p_seed;``, this would make ``gpu_particles_3d.cpp`` out of sync with the rendering server.  The ``get_seed`` function would no longer correctly reflect the value that has been set on the rendering server.  What are your thoughts on this?  @QbieShay Do you have some input as well?
We'll send it as-is; it'll be easy to apply a fix if this does cause a desync.
